```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(plotly)
library(gapminder)
```

# A Tiny Observatory

**Created: 27 October 2026**

Explore the relationship between national income and life expectancy. Each bubble is a country, size represents population, and colour represents continent. Hover over bubbles for details and use the year slider to explore change over time.

```{r interactive-plot}
gm <- gapminder::gapminder
plot_ly(data = gm, x = ~gdpPercap, y = ~lifeExp, size = ~pop,
        color = ~continent, frame = ~year,
        text = ~paste0("<b>", country, "</b><br>Year: ", year,
          "<br>Continent: ", continent,
          "<br>Population: ", format(pop, big.mark = ","),
          "<br>GDP per capita: $", round(gdpPercap, 0),
          "<br>Life expectancy: ", round(lifeExp, 1), " years"),
        hoverinfo = "text", type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(opacity = 0.72, sizemode = "area", sizeref = 2.5)) |>
  layout(title = list(text = "Life expectancy, income, and population over time"),
         xaxis = list(title = "GDP per capita (US dollars, log scale)", type = "log"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Life expectancy (years)", range = c(20, 90)),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "Continent"))) |>
  animation_opts(frame = 700, transition = 250, redraw = FALSE) |>
  animation_slider(currentvalue = list(prefix = "Year: ")) |>
  animation_button(x = 1, xanchor = "right", y = 0, yanchor = "bottom")
```

## What to look for

- **The broad upward pattern:** countries with higher GDP per capita often have higher life expectancy, although income alone does not explain health outcomes.
- **Differences between continents:** the point clouds overlap, but regions show different historical trajectories.
- **Population scale:** larger bubbles represent more people.
- **Change over time:** use the animation controls to compare years from 1952 to 2007.

This is an exploratory visualization, not a causal analysis. Country-level averages cannot be used to infer an individual person's health.

## Data source

Gapminder country-level data distributed in the R package `gapminder`. Interactive chart built with Plotly for R Markdown.
